Read every control of the native Moodle course settings form for one course: full name, short name, ID number, start and end dates, the course format and the options that format offers, appearance, files and uploads, completion tracking defaults, groups, tags and course custom fields. It returns the values the current form carries, the option list of each control the form offers, whether each native file area is empty, the exact protected-setting values, and the digest an approved settings or format change is compared against. It requires the moodle/course:update capability at that exact course context. Course visibility, the course summary and the course category are reported here but changed elsewhere: visibility through moodle_show_course and moodle_hide_course, and the summary through moodle_update_course_summary. Morrow has no course category move and no course deletion. It reads no student name, no student grade and no student submission.

Change a bounded set of settings on one exact Moodle course through its native course settings form: full name, short name, ID number, start and end dates, download content, relative dates mode, the options of the format the course already uses, appearance, files and uploads, completion tracking defaults, groups, tags and course custom fields. Morrow reloads the exact form after the reviewed read, carries every other control of that form through unchanged, sends one POST, then reads the saved form back and compares both the changed settings and a protected digest of every setting this change did not name. It refuses any value the current native control does not offer or cannot carry, and it refuses before sending anything when a native file area on the form, such as the course image, is not empty or cannot be proved empty, because one POST of this form would replace that area. It does not change the course format, the course visibility, the course summary or the course category. A lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried. It requires the moodle/course:update capability at that exact course context.

Morrow reads the complete course state before the change, reloads the exact settings form, sends one POST, reads the saved form back, then reads the complete course state again and reports both states with the format before and after. It also requires the course name, short name, ID number, visibility, summary and dates to come back unchanged. A lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried. It requires mod/assign:grade at that exact module context, binds the module through the native course/modedit.php Assignment form, and never opens /mod/assign/view.php or /mod/assign/grade.php. It refuses a group submission. The learner identity crosses the normal Moodle roster privacy boundary and is returned only as a stable learner token; a user who is absent from the complete course participant roster is refused before the result is returned. It returns no feedback comment text, no file bytes, no file URL, no grader identity, and no name, email, or session key. Read bounded aggregate discussion and reply counts for one exact Moodle Forum. The bridge binds the selected course module to its native Forum instance through the course/modedit.php Forum form, then pages Moodle's read-only discussion service and counts only discussion identities and reply totals in the browser. It requires the mod/forum:viewdiscussion capability at that exact module context, and it counts only the discussions the signed-in principal is permitted to see. It never opens /mod/forum/view.php or /mod/forum/discuss.php, and it never returns discussion rows, subjects, messages, author names, IDs, emails, attachments, group values, or unread state. It re-checks the approval window before each native request and before returning the counts, and refuses with moodle_forum_activity_summary_context_changed when the window has passed or the signed-in page context changed.

Change a bounded set of settings on one exact Moodle grade category through its native form: the aggregation method, the drop-lowest count, and the category weight in its parent. Morrow reloads the exact form, carries every other successful control unchanged, sends one POST, requires the native gradebook setup redirect, then reads the saved form back and compares both the changed settings and a protected digest of every setting this change did not name. A weight change also sets the native weight override that Moodle requires before it saves a weight; Morrow refuses the weight when the loaded form does not offer both controls, which is the case for the course category and for a category whose parent does not use natural weighting. It refuses any value the loaded control does not offer or cannot carry. When Moodle recomputes the category total from a new aggregation, the saved form no longer matches the protected digest, and Morrow reports the change as applied but unconfirmed rather than claiming it changed only what was asked. It never reads or changes student grades or grade values.

operations.summary: Change Moodle manual grade item settings
operations.description: Change a bounded set of settings on one exact Moodle manual grade item through its native form: the grade type, the maximum grade, the minimum grade, the display type, the decimal places, and the parent category. Morrow reloads the exact form, carries every other successful control unchanged, sends one POST, requires the native gradebook setup redirect, then reads the saved form back and compares both the changed settings and a protected digest of every setting this change did not name. It refuses every non-manual item, so external, category-total, and course-total items are refused, and it refuses any value the loaded control does not offer or cannot carry. Moodle's native item form offers its rescale control only for an item that already has grades: when that control is present, Morrow refuses a maximum-grade or minimum-grade change unless the request names the effect on those grades as rescale or keep, and it refuses every grade-type change. It also refuses a grade-type change to or from the scale grade type, because Moodle removes the rescale control for a scale item and the form then cannot say whether that item has grades. Morrow never reads a stored grade, so it reports the rescale effect it sent and makes no claim about the grades themselves.

Read the native Moodle scales page of one signed-in course and return each listed scale with its option labels, and, for a scale the page exposes an edit control for, its identity and whether a grade item already uses it. It requires the moodle/course:managescales capability at that exact course context. The page does not mark course scales apart from site scales in a language-independent way, so the result claims no scope for either list; a scale the signed-in user cannot manage here is returned with its name and options only. The result excludes student names, student grades, and stored grade values.

Read the native Moodle outcomes page of one signed-in course and return the course outcomes with their identity, full name, short name, scale name, and grade-item use count, plus the site outcomes with their name, short name, scale name, course use count, and grade-item use count. It requires the moodle/grade:manageoutcomes capability at that exact course context, and the site must have outcomes enabled; when outcomes are disabled the native page redirects and the read returns moodle_gradebook_read_unavailable. A site outcome is returned without an identity, because the native page exposes one only to a user who can manage site outcomes. The result excludes student names, student grades, and stored grade values.

Read the native Moodle course grade settings form of one signed-in course and return every setting it would save: grade display type, decimal points, aggregation position, the minimum and maximum source, and each grade report, import, and export plugin setting, with the selected option label the form shows for each menu. It requires the moodle/grade:manage capability at that exact course context. Per-category and per-item aggregation, weights, ranges, display type, decimals, hidden and locked flags, and category totals stay in moodle_get_grade_category and moodle_get_grade_item. The result excludes student names, student grades, and stored grade values.

operations.summary: Enumerate stored Moodle Question Bank references for one course

operations.summary: Read a Moodle Forum posting target
operations.description: Read the exact Moodle Forum that a discussion or post change will bind to, and optionally one exact discussion in it. The bridge binds the selected course module to its native Forum instance through the course/modedit.php Forum form and reports whether learners can see the Forum. When a discussion is named, it reads that discussion through Moodle's own mod_forum_get_discussion_posts service, which states the Forum and the course the discussion belongs to, and returns each post's ID, parent post, subject, deleted state, private-reply state, and attachment count. It requires mod/forum:viewdiscussion at that exact module context. It returns no author name, no author ID, and no post body, and it never opens /mod/forum/view.php or /mod/forum/discuss.php. Its digest covers the course, module, Forum, learner visibility, and discussion identity only, so a new reply between the review and the approval does not invalidate an approved change.

Start one discussion in one exact Moodle Forum through the native /mod/forum/post.php form. The subject and the HTML message are written by the approving person; Morrow never composes them from course content. It requires mod/forum:startdiscussion at that exact module context, refuses any draft file area on the native form that is not proven empty, refuses a message that names a Moodle file, reloads the form immediately before dispatch, and sends exactly one POST. It then reads back the discussions the signed-in person has posted in and requires exactly one new discussion whose single post carries the approved subject and message with no attachment. learner_visibility_confirmed must be true. A lost or unreadable response is reported as sent with an unknown outcome, and Morrow never sends it again.

operations.summary: Read one exact Moodle Quiz attempt record
operations.description: Read one exact Moodle Quiz attempt from Moodle's own Grades report route, /mod/quiz/report.php with mode=overview: the attempt state, the started, completed and duration text exactly as Moodle rendered it, and one record for each question slot carrying the question state and the mark Moodle displayed. It requires mod/quiz:viewreports at that exact module context, which is what Moodle requires to open that report, and it binds the course and the module through the report page itself. It never opens /mod/quiz/attempt.php, /mod/quiz/review.php, or /mod/quiz/reviewquestion.php, so it continues no attempt and records no attempt review; the report route does record one report-viewed event for the signed-in teacher in the course log. It returns no response text, no feedback, no question name, no learner name, and no session key. operations.summary: Replace the file of a Moodle Resource
operations.description: Replace the saved file of one exact Moodle Resource with one reviewed local file of at most 1 MiB. Learner links, bookmarks and embedded references to the old file stop working once it is replaced, and Morrow cannot restore the old file. It requires moodle/course:manageactivities at that exact module context. It refuses a Resource that holds more than one file. It reads the exact Resource and its native private draft copy first, removes the old file from that draft area, uploads the reviewed file, and compares the staged draft bytes against the planned filename, byte length and SHA-256 before anything is saved. It then sends one native Save and return to course and compares the saved bytes through pluginfile.php. An uncertain upload stops before the save, an uncertain save stays unconfirmed, and neither is sent again. It never opens the Resource view. Byte equality does not establish learner access. The bridge carries one reviewed file of at most 1 MiB per message, so this is not general file support. Morrow's local file planner stages one exact replacement file for review before dispatch. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Byte equality does not establish learner access. Morrow's local file planner stages this exact ordered set of files for review before dispatch. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

The grouping description and ID number are carried through unchanged and cannot be set here. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

name.description: The grouping name to save. Plain text without <, >, &, " or '.

operations.summary: Set the groups of a Moodle grouping
operations.description: Set which groups of one exact Moodle course belong to one exact grouping, through that grouping's own native group-assignment form. Requires moodle/course:managegroups at the course context. Moodle's own form adds groups or removes them in one submission, never both, and Morrow sends one POST, so a requested set that both adds and removes groups is refused with moodle_grouping_groups_two_directions and has to be sent as two approved changes. Every requested group must be a group of this course. Morrow reads every grouping of the course, requires the digest of that reading, reads the grouping's own assignment form immediately before it acts, sends one POST with Moodle's own add or remove control, and then requires the groupings back with exactly the requested group set on that grouping and every other grouping unchanged. A lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried. Changing a grouping changes which learners an activity that uses it can reach. It moves no learner between groups and removes no group. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

group_ids.description: The complete set of course group IDs this grouping should hold.

operations.summary: Set one Moodle activity's group mode
operations.description: Set the group mode of one exact activity with the same native course-format action the course page's own group-mode control uses. That action requires moodle/course:manageactivities at the course context, not moodle/course:managegroups. Separate groups means each learner sees only their own group's work in that activity; visible groups means each learner works in their own group but can see the others; no groups means the activity has no group behaviour. A course can force its own group mode on every activity, and that forced mode overrides what is saved here, so Morrow reads the course setting as well and reports both the value it saved and the mode that is actually in effect. Morrow reads the complete course state and the course setting, reads both again immediately before it acts, sends one native action, then requires the complete course state back with exactly that group mode on that activity and every other activity, section and course field unchanged. A lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried. It changes no group, no membership and no grouping. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

group_mode.description: 0 no groups, 1 separate groups, 2 visible groups.

operations.description: Read the bounded aggregate activity report for one exact Moodle course: for each activity, the course-module ID, the module type, and the number of views Moodle's own outline report shows for it, plus the course total. It requires report/outline:view at that exact course context. It reads /report/outline/index.php with the course id only; opening it records Moodle's own report_viewed log event for you, exactly as opening the report in Moodle does, and changes no learner state. The outline report lists no learner, so this result carries no learner row, name, or ID. It bounds the response to 2 MiB and the course to 500 activities, and returns moodle_course_activity_report_incomplete instead of a partial report when a bound is exceeded. An activity whose views cell is not a plain number is returned with no count and is included in unreadable_count; no value is inferred. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Read Moodle's native participation report for one exact activity in one exact course over a stated number of days: how many of the listed people did the chosen action, how many did not, and how many times in total. It requires report/participation:view at that exact course context. It reads /report/participation/index.php with the course id, the course-module id, the action, the time window and a page number; opening it records Moodle's own report_viewed log event for you and changes no learner state. It is aggregate by default and names nobody. Set include_participants to true to also get one row per listed person; each identity is then returned only as a stable learner token, and a person the complete course participant roster does not hold refuses the whole report. It bounds each response to 2 MiB, caps the report at 5000 people and 100 page requests, and returns moodle_course_participation_report_incomplete instead of a partial report when a bound is exceeded or when it does not reach the report's own last page. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Read the bounded aggregate result of Moodle's own Activity completion report for one exact course: for each completion-tracked activity, the course-module ID, the module type, and how many of the listed people it shows as complete, as incomplete, and as neither. It requires report/progress:view at that exact course context. It reads /report/progress/index.php with the course id and a page number only; opening it records Moodle's own report_viewed log event for you and changes no completion state. It returns no learner row, name, or ID. A completion cell is counted only from the toggle control Moodle renders for a person who may override completion; a pass or fail cell, and any cell without that control, is counted in unreadable_count instead of being guessed from a themed and translated icon. It bounds each response to 2 MiB, caps the course at 5000 people, 500 activities and 200 page requests, and returns moodle_course_completion_report_incomplete instead of a partial report when a bound is exceeded or when it does not reach the report's own last page. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Read a bounded aggregate summary of one exact Moodle course's log: how many entries were read, how many of them happened in each activity, how many at the course itself, and how many came from each request origin Moodle records (web, web service, command line, restore). It requires report/log:view at that exact course context. It reads /report/log/index.php with the course id, a page number and a page size; opening it records Moodle's own report_viewed log event for you and changes no learner state. Moodle's log table renders an IP address column, and a log store can add a user agent column of its own. This read parses two cells of each row, the activity context and the request origin, and never reads the time, user, related user, component, event name, description, IP address, or user agent cells, so none of them can appear in the result. It returns no learner row, name, or ID. It bounds each response to 2 MiB, caps the summary at 5000 entries and 50 page requests, and returns moodle_course_log_summary_incomplete instead of a partial summary when a bound is exceeded or when it does not reach the log's own last page. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Count the dated entries in one exact Moodle course's calendar, month by month, for a run of up to twelve months from the year and month you name: how many dated entries each month holds, how many belong to each activity, how many are course events, and how many personal or group entries were dropped. Moodle 5.2.2 ships no core dates report; the Dates report teachers may know is the third-party report_editdates plugin, so no report capability gates this read. It uses the core calendar month view service core_calendar_get_calendar_monthly_view, which lib/db/services.php registers as an AJAX read, and it returns only what the signed-in person can already see in this course's calendar. It returns counts only: no date, no event name and no learner row, name or ID. A civil date needs the signed-in person's time zone, so use moodle_list_course_events when you need each entry with the civil values Moodle itself rendered. Moodle's month grid repeats a multi-day entry on every day it covers, so each entry is counted once, in the first month of the window that shows it. It bounds each response to 2 MiB, caps the read at 12 months, 2000 entries and 500 activities, and returns moodle_course_dates_report_incomplete instead of a partial report when a bound is exceeded. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

Read the backup file areas of one exact Moodle course from its native restore page: the course backup area, the user private backup area and, where the site keeps them, the automated backup area. For each file it returns the area, the file name, the time Moodle shows for it, the size Moodle shows for it, whether that file offers a Restore link, whether it is a backup that is still running, and a digest that names that exact file for a later restore. It also reports how many restores are already running in this course and whether the site runs backups and restores as scheduled tasks. It requires the moodle/restore:restorecourse capability at that exact course context. The file's own download address and the file hashes Moodle uses to identify it stay in the browser and never appear in a result. It reads no student name, no student grade and no student submission.

Read the current status of one Moodle course backup that the site is running as a scheduled task, named by the operation ID that moodle_start_course_backup or moodle_list_backup_files returned. It reports the Moodle status code, the state that code means (preparing, queued, running, failed or complete), the fraction Moodle reports as done, and whether the operation has finished. Morrow makes exactly one request for exactly one operation ID: it does not wait, does not poll in a loop and does not retry, so ask again to see a later status. It refuses an ID that belongs to a restore. It requires the moodle/backup:backupcourse capability at that exact course context, which is what Moodle's own progress service checks.

operation_id.description: The backup operation ID Moodle returned when the backup started.

operations.description: Read the current status of one Moodle course restore that the site is running as a scheduled task, named by the operation ID that moodle_start_course_restore returned. It reports the Moodle status code, the state that code means (preparing, queued, running, failed or complete), the fraction Moodle reports as done, and whether the operation has finished. Morrow makes exactly one request for exactly one operation ID: it does not wait, does not poll in a loop and does not retry, so ask again to see a later status. It refuses an ID that belongs to a backup. It requires the moodle/backup:backupcourse capability at that exact course context, which is what Moodle's own progress service checks.

operation_id.description: The restore operation ID Moodle returned when the restore was queued.

operations.description: Start a backup of one exact Moodle course through its native backup form, using Moodle's own Jump to final step with the backup settings that form already carries. Morrow reads the course backup file areas first, reloads the form, sends one POST, then reads the file areas again and requires exactly one new entry and nothing removed. The result names the new backup file, the operation ID to ask for progress with, and every setting it sent. It refuses before sending when a backup of this course is already running, and when the site does not run backups as scheduled tasks, because the other route would run the whole backup inside one request and a browser can resend a request whose connection drops. A lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried. It requires the moodle/backup:backupcourse capability at that exact course context. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

operations.summary: Restore a Moodle backup into this course
operations.description: Restore one exact backup file into the approved Moodle course, through Moodle's own restore stages. This is a whole-course change. With restore_mode merge, the backup is added to what the course already holds. With restore_mode delete_and_restore, Moodle removes everything the course holds first and then restores the backup over the empty course: every section, every activity and every learner record in it, including submissions, attempts, grades, posts and files. Morrow cannot undo either mode. The approval names the exact source file, by name and by the digest moodle_list_backup_files returned for it, the exact target course, and the restore mode, and delete_and_restore also requires acknowledge_delete_and_restore. Morrow opens that file's own native Restore link, opens the destination stage, then sends the destination, settings, schema and review stages as four separate steps, each dispatched once and each checked against the stage Moodle answers with. The restore is then queued as a scheduled task, so nothing in the course has changed when this returns; ask moodle_get_restore_progress for the rest. A step whose answer is lost is reported as applied but unconfirmed and is never retried, and no later step is sent. A stage Moodle does not answer as promised ends the native workflow with its own Cancel. It refuses before sending when a restore is already running in this course, and when the site does not run restores as scheduled tasks. It requires the moodle/restore:restorecourse capability at that exact course context. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

source_file_name.description: The exact backup file name moodle_list_backup_files returned.

source_file_digest.description: The file_digest moodle_list_backup_files returned for that exact file.

restore_mode.description: merge adds the backup to the course. delete_and_restore removes everything in the course first.

acknowledge_course_change.description: Confirms that this changes the whole course and that Morrow cannot undo it.

acknowledge_delete_and_restore.description: Required only for delete_and_restore, and refused for merge. Confirms that everything in the course is removed first.

operations.summary: Import another course into this Moodle course
operations.description: Copy the content of one other Moodle course into the approved course, through the native import form, using Moodle's own Jump to final step with the import settings that form already carries. It adds to the approved course and does not delete anything in it: Morrow uses only Moodle's merging import target. It carries no learner data, because Moodle locks user data out of an import. Morrow reads the complete course state before the import, reads it again immediately before the one POST and refuses when it changed, sends one POST, then reads the complete course state again and reports both with the activities the import added. Moodle runs an import inside that one request, so a large source course can take a long time. A result with no added activity is reported as applied but unconfirmed rather than as a success, and a lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed; neither is retried. It requires the moodle/restore:restoretargetimport capability at the approved course and the moodle/backup:backuptargetimport capability at the source course. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it. The required expected_digest must match the canonical 64-character lowercase SHA-256 digest of the complete snapshot from moodle_get_contents, and Morrow compares that snapshot again immediately before send.

source_course_id.description: The course to copy content from. It cannot be the approved course itself.

acknowledge_course_change.description: Confirms that this adds content to the whole course and that Morrow cannot undo it.

expected_digest.description: The canonical SHA-256 digest of the complete snapshot from moodle_get_contents.

operations.summary: Copy a Moodle course into a new course
operations.description: Create a new Moodle course from the approved course, through the native course copy form. The copy is always created hidden, so it cannot reach a learner before someone shows it, and it always carries no learner data and keeps no enrolments, because Morrow copies no people. Morrow refuses before sending when the form already keeps a role's enrolments. The copy is created without an ID number unless you give one, because Moodle refuses a course whose ID number is already in use and the form is seeded with the source course's own. Every other control of the form, including the dates it offers, is sent back unchanged. Morrow reads the course copies already in progress first, refuses a copy whose new full name is already being made, sends one POST, then reads the copies again and requires exactly one new copy with that exact name. Moodle makes the copy as scheduled tasks, so the new course is not finished when this returns. A short name Moodle already uses is refused by the native form and is reported as sent but not applied; a lost response is reported as applied but unconfirmed. Neither is retried. It requires moodle/backup:backupcourse, moodle/restore:restorecourse and moodle/course:create at that exact course context. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it. The required expected_digest must match the canonical 64-character lowercase SHA-256 digest of the complete snapshot from moodle_get_course_settings, and Morrow compares that snapshot again immediately before send.

category_id.description: A category the native control offers. Without it the copy keeps the source course's category.

new_id_number.description: Optional. Without it the copy is created with no ID number.

acknowledge_new_course.description: Confirms that this creates a new course, which Morrow cannot delete.

expected_digest.description: The canonical SHA-256 digest of the complete snapshot from moodle_get_course_settings.

operations.summary: Get the Moodle release and the installed plugin inventory
operations.description: Read this Moodle site's release and its installed plugin inventory: each plugin's type, name, component and version number, and the enabled or disabled state Moodle itself shows for it. The inventory is site-wide; course_id names the selected course whose signed-in site connection Morrow reads through, and the result carries no course content. The enabled authentication, enrolment, question-bank filter, availability condition, repository and filter plugins are reported as their own sets, read from those same rows. Morrow reads two native administration pages and sends nothing: /admin/environment.php for the release, which requires moodle/site:config at the system context, and /admin/plugins.php for the inventory, which Moodle serves only to a site administrator. When either page is not served, Morrow returns moodle_site_inventory_administration_required and reports no inventory; it never treats a page it could not read as an empty site. Morrow cannot tell a person who is not an administrator from a site that changed these pages, and refuses in both cases. No secret leaves the page: every value is rebuilt from a fixed vocabulary, and the plugin display name, settings link, uninstall link, update control and notes are never read, so no API key, token, password, session key or salted value can reach the result. A row carrying a class this read does not recognise is refused as moodle_site_inventory_page_control_unrecognised. This adds no administration write: Morrow cannot enable, disable, install, update or remove a plugin. It bounds the response to 2 MiB and the site to 2000 plugins and returns moodle_site_inventory_incomplete instead of a partial inventory. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

operations.summary: Get Moodle role short names and one role's archetype and context overrides
operations.description: Read every Moodle role's ID and short name, and, when one role is named, that role's archetype and the capability overrides Moodle shows for it at the selected course's own context. Morrow reads native administration pages and sends nothing: /admin/roles/manage.php for the role list, which requires moodle/role:manage at the system context; /admin/roles/define.php for the archetype, which requires the same capability and saves nothing when it is only rendered; and /admin/roles/override.php for the overrides at this course context, which requires moodle/role:override, or moodle/role:safeoverride, at that exact context. When Moodle does not serve the role list, Morrow returns moodle_role_definitions_administration_required and reports no role, because these pages reach a site administrator or a person holding that exact system-context capability. Morrow cannot tell a person who is not an administrator from a site that changed these pages, and refuses in both cases. When Moodle serves the role list but not the override form, the overrides stay unknown: the result reports context_overrides_visible false and context_overrides null, never an empty list. An override is a capability whose permission at this context is allow, prevent or prohibit; inherit is no override. A permission or archetype value this read does not recognise is refused as moodle_role_definitions_page_control_unrecognised. No secret leaves the page: the role display name, role description, action links and every hidden form control, including the session key, are never read. This adds no administration write: Morrow cannot create, change, delete, assign or override a role. It bounds the response to 2 MiB, the site to 200 roles, and one role to 5000 capability rows and 500 overrides, and returns moodle_role_definitions_incomplete instead of a partial answer. Browser-fixture proof only; no signed-in Moodle site has run it.

role_id.description: Optional. Without it the result lists every role and opens no role definition.
